fields.v: Minn, W., Sun, Z., Shar, L. K., Lo, D. (2026). SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents. arXiv:2610.12569v1 [cs.CL], 8 Oct 2026 (under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027)
Preprint — arXiv:2610.12569v1 [cs.CL]; header 'Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027', not yet accepted
School of Computing and Information Systems, Singapore Management University (all four authors; academic)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — self-scaling arena SWE-Duel in which coding agents create (Red) and solve (Blue) feature-plus-hidden-bug pull requests for each other, with a 1,500-turn round-robin tournament among 11 model-harness participants, a harness ablation tournament and validation studies

No SDD approach. Participants (model + harness): GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, Kimi K2.7 Code, DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.2, Qwen 3.7 Max, Nemotron 3 Ultra, MiniMax M3, Gemini 3.1 Pro (late entrant), each with mini-swe-agent; GPT-5.5 with Codex CLI; Claude Opus 4.8 with Claude Code. Harness ablation adds DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.2, Kimi K2.7 Code under Codex CLI and Claude Code; difficulty ladder GLM-5.1/5.2/5.3. Models via OpenRouter (IDs and access dates given, Table 5); harness versions Not stated; temperature 0.2

N/A (no approach). Task tuple produced by the Red agent: feature specification s, pull-request diff d (feature plus embedded bug), feature test suite Tf and sealed bug test suite Tb; Blue receives repository, s, d and Tf only

N/A for an SDD approach. Arena protocol: Red Session A feature implementation (gate A: existing and feature tests pass, size thresholds), Session B bug embedding (gate B: build and visible tests pass, Tb passes on feature-only diff and fails on d), Session C blind self-repair by a fresh instance of the same participant (gate C: all three suites pass); up to 5 attempts per slot; Blue then reviews the PR without being told of a bug and wins only if existing, feature and bug tests all pass
N/A (fully automated; no human in the loop). Post-hoc manual audit of 50 bug-test-only losses
N/A — no SDD approach run; agents author feature specifications, code and tests and review each other's pull requests

Existing code bases: agent-authored feature additions with embedded bugs on pinned open-source repositories; Blue performs code review, fault localisation and repair

Bradley-Terry log-strength rating with bootstrap rank probabilities and 95% CIs; match W/D/L; task admission yield; self-repair stability rate; sealed-test false-negative rate; fixed-reference solver failure rate; rank correlations (Spearman, Kendall's τ)

Automatic: test suites executed in per-repository Docker containers by validation gates and turn scorers; Bradley-Terry fitted by maximum likelihood with 1,000 bootstrap resamples of matches; API cost and tokens recorded. Manual: audit of a seeded random sample of 50 of 158 turns lost only on the bug tests. Additional studies: 3 re-runs of self-repair on 44 sampled tasks; fixed-reference solver (GLM-5.2) on all 134 tasks; Wilson intervals, exact trend and Fisher tests

Main tournament, 15 repositories, one run per turn; criterion per turn: Blue wins iff existing, feature and bug tests all pass; no threshold for a configuration verdict. Red win % / Blue win % / Bradley-Terry / total API cost (Tables 1, 12): (a) GPT-5.5 + Codex CLI: 11.3 / 98.7 / +2.82 / $641.89. (b) Claude Opus 4.8 + mini-swe-agent: 27.3 / 88.7 / +2.46 / $223.59. (c) GPT-5.5 + mini-swe-agent: 10.4 / 97.0 / +2.13 / $247.18. (d) Kimi K2.7 Code + mini-swe-agent: 15.6 / 90.4 / +1.82 / $92.39. (e) DeepSeek V4 Pro + mini-swe-agent: 18.5 / 91.9 / +1.50 / $67.07. (f) GLM-5.2 + mini-swe-agent: 14.8 / 89.6 / +1.19 / $104.97. (g) Qwen3.7 Max + mini-swe-agent: 13.3 / 91.1 / +0.49 / $107.22. (h) Claude Opus 4.8 + Claude Code: 7.3 / 87.3 / −1.41 / $179.05. (i) Nemotron 3 Ultra + mini-swe-agent: 6.7 / 79.3 / −2.60 / $171.34. (j) MiniMax M3 + mini-swe-agent: 2.0 / 74.7 / −3.86 / $86.77. (k) Gemini 3.1 Pro + mini-swe-agent (late entrant, 5 matches, 0-1-4): 2.7 / 72.0 / −4.55 / $187.76; contested Blue success 61.8%. Fixed-reference solver failure on each author's tasks: (b) 26.7%, (e) 20.0%, (g) 20.0%, (i) 14.3%, (f)/(a)/(c) 7.7%, (h) 6.7%, (d)/(j)/(k) 0.0%. Harness ablation (3 models pooled), score rate: (l) mini-swe-agent 0.52 [0.43, 0.60], BT +0.73; (m) Codex CLI 0.50 [0.42, 0.60], BT −0.25; (n) Claude Code 0.48 [0.40, 0.58], BT −0.49 (ablation). Each configuration: quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors

Tasks: authored at evaluation time by the participants themselves (Red), validated by three executable gates and blind self-repair, stored in task banks so every opponent faces the same tasks from a given Red; 15 repositories pinned to commits. Configurations: 11 model-harness participants, 10 in a full round robin (45 matches) plus a late entrant playing 5 active-sampled incumbents. Baseline: none external; fixed-reference solver (GLM-5.2 + mini-swe-agent) puts all authors on one scale. Held constant: Docker image per repository, prompts, 50-step budget per session plus up to 3 recovery turns of 6 steps, 30-min wall-clock limit, temperature 0.2, OpenRouter endpoint; step counts do not equalise compute. Acceptance tests: existing, feature and sealed bug suites. Repetitions: one run per turn; admission stability re-run 3 times on 44 tasks. Missing Red tasks scored as Blue wins (also reported without). Human intervention: none. Harness ablation: same model under three harnesses, round robin within model

GPT-5.5 + Codex CLI ranks first (BT +2.82; strongest solver), Claude Opus 4.8 + mini-swe-agent second (strongest task author, Red win 27.3%); six leaders form a broad group with overlapping CIs; Claude Opus 4.8 + Claude Code ranks 8th. Blue succeeds in 87.9% of all turns and 85.1% of contested turns (1,037 clean repairs, 158 shipped bugs, 24 collapses); by language Java 89.2% to Node 82.9%; logic errors hardest (81.9%). Fixed-reference Red win rates correlate with tournament rates (Spearman ρ = 0.66). Late entrant placed with 5 matches without changing incumbent order (Kendall τ = 1.0). Difficulty ladder: fixed solver fails 8.3% (GLM-5.1), 0.0% (GLM-5.2), 42.9% (GLM-5.3) of tasks, trend p = .015; newest vs pooled older 42.9% vs 4.0% (Fisher p = .005). Harness ablation: no harness ordering resolved (intervals overlap; pairwise margins +2, +2, −8 of 90 turns, all CIs include 0). Cost: $2,109 total, about $26 per match; GPT-5.5 + Codex the most expensive ($641.89, 2.6× the next)

Partly to yes, by the authors' account: the arena separated participants by Bradley-Terry rating and by role profile, placed a newcomer cheaply, and the fixed-solver and ladder studies support that difficulty rises with author capability (preliminary). Checks: self-repair stability 91.7% pooled (35/44 tasks repaired in all 3 re-runs, one in none); sealed bug tests false-negative rate 6.0% (3 of 50 audited). Limits stated: task difficulty capped by the author's own bug-finding ability (self-repair gate); ranks of the leading group overlap; harness ablation cannot resolve differences below about 0.2 score-rate points; ladder has 12-14 tasks per level and one draw per task, so adjacent versions are not resolved; native harness pairings in the main tournament are not a harness probe; harness steps do not equalise compute

No dedicated limitations section; limitations stated across the paper: difficulty bounded by the author's own repair ability (deliberate solvability/difficulty trade-off); agent-written sealed tests can reject valid repairs (6.0% false negatives); admission by a single stochastic self-repair run; small ladder and harness-ablation samples; released task banks become retired once public (freshness renewed only by new banks); dual-use risk of generating CI-evading defects (ethics statement). Gaps: static benchmarks leak and saturate; benchmarks need tasks and oracles created at evaluation time with difficulty set by the participants

Toolkit and experiment dataset open-sourced (https://sweduel.github.io/SWE-Duel; Minn 2026a, 2026c); task banks of a tournament should be retired once disclosed. No pre-registration. Languages: Python, Go, JavaScript (Node), Java, C, C++. Reporting: abstract and conclusion give GPT-5.5 + Codex CLI 'repairing 98.3% of the defects it reviews', which is its contested-turn Blue success (Table 13: 0.983, 120 turns), whereas Table 1 gives the full-schedule Blue win rate 98.7% (missing-Red auto-wins included); both values are used here with that distinction. Abstract says the newest version's tasks defeat 'a fixed-reference solver', the introduction 'a fixed reviewer' (DeepSeek-V4-Pro + mini-swe-agent in the ladder, GLM-5.2 + mini-swe-agent for the tournament tasks). Appendix K calls the ladder result 'direct evidence' while the abstract says 'preliminary evidence'. Table 1 W/D/L columns are garbled in the text extraction (only Gemini's 0-1-4 confirmed in the text). Ethics statement on dual use; all runs in isolated local containers, no PRs to real repositories

fields.why: Judgement: the abstract and conclusion hedge, but Appendix K (p. 32) presents the small ladder (39 tasks, one solver draw each) as 'direct evidence' of the self-scaling property; another reader could score Partly for that overclaim.
fields.doubt: O resumo diz 'preliminary evidence', mas o Apêndice K (p. 32) chama 'direct evidence' a uma escada de só 39 tarefas com uma execução cada; decide se isso baixa Q9 para Partly.
